June 2024

Examiners' Checklist

Key areas to assessScoreDonePartially doneNot done
1The in charge stays calm but acts quickly1
2Determines casualty's unresponsiveness, checks for breathing and carotid pulse1
3Calls for support from colleagues, by activating the code for emergencies1
4Gives clear instructions to the junior colleagues after confirming whether they can do CPR1
5Co-ordinates with the 2 to lift casualty onto a firm flat surface½x
6Orders the staff to bring the emergency tray½x
7In-charge kneels by the casualty's side, tilts head lifting chin as the colleague inserts airway2
8In-charge coordinates with the staff who is conversant with CPR to form a seal over the patient's mouth and nose and inflate, as the in-charge starts on the compressions2
9The second colleague re-assesses the casualty for breathing and circulation½x
10In-charge records procedure as the other 2 colleagues are instructed to clear away and leave patient comfortable½x

Examiners' Checklist

Key areas to assessScoreDonePartially doneNot done
1Creates rapport with the client and ensures privacy.½x
2Shows empathy and concern for the client's ordeal.½x
3Commends her for the decision to seek care.½x
4Takes a brief history of the sexual assault to confirm penetration and whether it was the first time she has had this experience.½x
5Explains to her how ECPs work to prevent pregnancy.1
6Provides ECPs - Example Postinor (Levonegesterol) 2 pills or 8 pills of COCs and explains how to take them. If possible offers the first dose of Directly Observed Treatment (DOT) before she leaves the clinic.2
7Counsels her on other treatments like Post Exposure Prophylaxis to prevent against HIV infection and also other STIs.1
8Counsels her on possible side effects of ECPs.1
9Asks her to consider involving the police.1
10Refers her to a professional counselor.½x
11Advises her to come back after 4 weeks to rule out pregnancy and schedules return date.1
12Documents the findings.½x
